Trump, Putin reach deal to release Russian diesel to world
item.description:
US President Donald Trump on Friday said Russian President Vladimir Putin had agreed to release Russian diesel to US and global markets.
The move, which aims to address rising fuel costs before the US midterm elections, marks a dramatic turnaround in US policy toward Moscow since the start of the war in Ukraine.
In a social media post, Trump wrote he had made a deal with Putin during a phone call that was supposed to be about a suspected plague outbreak in Russia.
According to Trump, Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, followed by an additional 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons “immediately thereafter.”
Trump wrote that Russia would deliver another 3 million tons “within a short period of time” after that.
The US Treasury Department issued a temporary license that will allow Russian diesel to reach global markets through April 2027.
Trump’s announcement follows his signing of a broad Russia sanctions law last month. The law is intended to clamp down on Russia’s energy sector and other areas that fuel its war against Ukraine.
Kirill Dmitriev, the Russian presidential envoy, reposted the Treasury Department’s announcement on X, saying that “Russia-US cooperation on diesel and energy will benefit the world.”
Alexander Novak, Russia’s Deputy Prime Minister, said that the country was ready to start supplying additional volumes of diesel to the United States and other countries from October.
He also said that Russia’s exports are expected to rise further in November and December as refineries resume operations after maintenance.
Later, the Kremlin released a statement from Putin saying that, during their call, he and Trump had also devoted “significant attention to the prospects of resolving the Ukrainian crisis” and had discussed “the situation around Iran and various aspects of bilateral relations.”
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has condemned the agreement, saying that any easing of sanctions without a clear and lasting de-escalation agreement with Russia is an obvious sign of “weakness.”
“Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world. Russia will ‘repay’ the diesel with further terror and perfidy,” he wrote on social media.
“Allowing Russia to ⁠sell ​petroleum products ​is an investment in a ​war that ‌must be ended, not prolonged. What ​is needed ⁠is real de-escalation with Russia ⁠on ​a reciprocal basis,” the Ukrainian president stressed.
Zelensky added that Ukraine hopes the US will have a strong conversation with Russia: “A strong one, not a weak one.”
Since its 2022 full-scale invasion of neighboring Ukraine, Moscow has been hit with rounds of sanctions by the United States and its Western partners.
But as the war has continued with no resolution in sight, Washington’s commitment to that approach has appeared to waver.
Earlier this year, temporary US sanctions waivers that allowed the sale of Russian oil raised concerns because they could hinder efforts to deprive Moscow of funds for its war in Ukraine.
Last month, Trump blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries for soaring diesel prices, and even publicly told Zelensky to stop the attacks.
Trump’s announcement on Friday came just as US, Ukrainian, and European officials were meeting in Miami for new diplomatic talks aimed at ending Russia’s war in Ukraine.

item.title: US announces sanctions on the International Criminal Court
item.description:
US President Donald Trump’s administration imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Friday, hours after one of its former judges won the Nobel Peace Prize.
This comes as the US has in recent months made no bones about pursuing what Secretary of State Marco Rubio has called a “sweeping campaign to dismantle the threat posed by the International Criminal Court.”
The United States and Israel had both strongly opposed the court’s arrest warrants for top Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Since 2020 and the back end of Trump’s first term, the US had also opposed investigations into military actions in Afghanistan that “deprioritize” alleged US wrongdoings, focusing on the Taliban, but can nevertheless include them.
“President Trump will never allow the International Court to prosecute Americans,” Rubio said in a statement.
“That is why, today, the United States is sanctioning the International Criminal Court. We will ban transactions with this rogue court, cutting off their resources and crippling its ability to operate,” he said.
Rubio said that both US political parties had long agreed that the ICC should not have jurisdiction over US citizens, but said “only President Trump” resolved to take action.
“Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC. We expect our allies, many of whom are part of the ICC and that rely on American servicemembers for their defense, to rein in the court,” Rubio said. “If they do not, the United States will continue its campaign to dismantle the ICC, brick by brick, until Americans are threatened no longer.”
The ICC said the US sanctions aimed to obstruct an independent international court supported by more than half of the UN’s members.
“The court will continue to fully discharge its mandate, with independence and impartiality, acting only on the basis of the law and the evidence, for the sake of the countless victims of grave crimes,” said ICC President Tomoko Akane, who already faces US sanctions.
The ICC called the Rome Statute, which underpins membership of the court, a “collective promise” that the most serious international crimes must not go unpunished.
“That promise is only as strong as the resolve of those who made it,” the court said. It appealed to members to take “concrete actions” to ensure the court would still have the necessary means to continue its work.
“No one should be punished for serving the cause of justice,” it said. “History will judge this moment. Future generations, and above all the victims of mass atrocities, will ask how we responded when an insitution created to protect them came under attack.”
A collection of US allies that are full members of the ICC including Germany issued a joint statement reaffirming their “continued and unwavering support for the independence, impartiality, and integrity of the ICC.”
“As committed supporters of the ICC we regret and strongly disagree with the announcement of sanctions to be imposed upon the Court by the United States,” the governments of Canada, Denmark, Germany, France, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands and the UK said.
They said that, despite the ICC’s best efforts to prepare and mitigate their effect, the sanctions “will have a significant impact on the Court’s work, its dedicated staff and their families.”
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu thanked the US government for its “leadership” in issuing the sanctions.
“The ICC is not a court. It is a political body that poses a mortal threat to law abiding democracies worldwide and to the very idea of national sovereignty,” he said.
The State Department released the announcement a few hours after the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Navi Pillay, who was an ICC judge from 2003 to 2012.
Last year Trump repeatedly complained that he should have won the accolade for promoting world peace, prompting Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado to present him with her trophy as a gift.
Without naming names, the Nobel Committee clearly referenced US sanctions against the ICC when announcing Pillay as this year’s laureate.
“The Norwegian Nobel Committee wants to remind the world that the rule of law national and international — underpins the system we have set up to ensure peace and resolve conflicts non-violently,” the Committee wrote.
It said judges like Pillay “guard the thin red line between order and chaos,” but lamented that “today ... these same judges are sanctioned, and their institutions are attacked.” The International Criminal Court is an intergovernmental organization and international tribunal based in the Dutch city of The Hague.
It’s the only permanent international court with the theoretical jurisdiction to prosecute individuals for international crimes like genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and illegal aggression.
The ICC was established in 2002 and is governed by the Rome Statute.
More than half the countries in the world, 125 in total, are full parties to the Rome Statute, having signed and ratified it.
Several of the world’s most significant powers, including China, India, Israel, Russia and the United States, do not recognize the court’s jurisdiction and are not parties to the statute.
A grey area, however, remains since the court accepts challenges from ratified members against individuals from countries that do not recognize it.
That is why high-profile arrest warrants against Russian officials, including President Vladimir Putin, and Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, have been issued in recent years — following respective complaints from Ukrainians and Palestinians.
The US has been increasingly critical of the ICC during Trump’s second term.
Rubio has often led the charge. In July, he wrote an op-ed for the Wall Street Journal saying, “America never agreed to a world tribunal that can override our own courts and the Constitution.”
He argued it was possible for US “soldiers, police officers, Border Patrol agents and elected leaders” to be “dragged before an international court” and tried by judges “from random countries across the globe.”
Just over a week later, on July 25, Venezuela’s new administration — transformed after the US abduction of Nicolas Maduro in January — announced that it planned to withdraw from the Rome Statute and the ICC.
A few days later, the military junta in Chad announced that it was withdrawing from the ICC following a US request.
The recent sexual misconduct scandal surrounding the ICC’s chief prosecutor Karim Khan, who was dismissed in July, provided more ammunition the US could aim at the court.
In August, the US imposed sanctions on the ICC’s president, Japanese judge Tomoko Akane, and Abdoulaye Seye, a Senegalese trial lawyer at the court.

item.title: Year later, Gaza ceasefire promises mostly unfulfilled
item.description:
One year after US President Donald Trump declared the war in Gaza to be over, few of the long-term promises of the ceasefire have come to fruition.
Here is a list of some of the key points of the October 10, 2025 ceasefire and where things stand:
Three days after the agreement was announced, Hamas freed the 20 remaining living hostages seized during the group’s October 7, 2023 resistance campaign.
The captives’ return was a key priority for Israel, whose public had agonized over their fate.
The ceasefire anniversary also marks one year of quiet for Israel from the Gaza front, with no rocket attacks by Hamas.
The group’s missile inventory was depleted by near-constant Israeli bombardment, which damaged or destroyed the vast majority of buildings in the Palestinian territory.
The US military set up a command post with foreign allies near the Gaza border to monitor the truce.
Israel has reduced its level of attacks but has kept striking Gaza on a near-daily basis.
Israeli strikes have killed some 1,450 Palestinians since the ceasefire, according to Gaza’s health ministry, which operates under Hamas and whose figures are considered accurate by the United Nations.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is in a tight election race, has vowed to kill everyone involved in the October 7 resistance campaign.
Netanyahu said on the attack’s anniversary that 4,000 out of 6,000 “Hamas monsters” had been killed.
Israeli forces were allowed to stay in 53% of Gaza under the terms of the ceasefire, but a year later they control about 70% of it, according to official accounts.
The second phase of the agreement was supposed to include a political transition away from Hamas, and technocrat Ali Shaath was appointed head of a new National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG).
Hamas announced in July that it was disbanding its governing body and handing over Gaza’s administration to the US-blessed NCAG.
But Hamas effectively remains in charge of security in Gaza, and Shaath has taken a low profile.
The Palestinian Islamist movement elected a new leader, Khalil al-Hayya, in July. Shortly afterwards, the group announced it would give up its weapons, a step hailed by Trump as a breakthrough.
But Israel has been sceptical, with Netanyahu demanding verifiable decommissioning of all weapons down to individual guns.
Hamas has not gone ahead with disarmament, and Israel has refused to reciprocate by starting to withdraw forces.
Trump set up a new global body for the deal dubbed the “Board of Peace,” tapping as key figures former British prime minister Tony Blair and Bulgarian diplomat Nickolay Mladenov, who serves as “Gaza high representative.”
Trump, a critic of foreign aid, in January promised $10 billion in US funding to the board he controls, and Gulf allies have pledged more, but no money is known to have made its way to Gaza reconstruction.
In September, the board proposed a $2.45 billion Gaza recovery plan at a meeting of its members and stakeholders, in an effort meant to span over six months.

item.title: Russian strikes kill 11 including 3 children
item.description:
Russian strikes on Ukraine’s southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia on Saturday killed at least 11 people, including three children, according to regional authorities.
Ukrainian national police said Russia had targeted residential neighborhoods in the city with “five guided aerial bombs” early Saturday morning, hitting two residential buildings.
The strikes came a day after Ukrainian and European officials met in Miami in a renewed diplomatic push to end Russia’s war in Ukraine.
“The toll from the air strikes on Zaporizhzhia continues to rise. At present, 11 civilians have been killed. Among them are three children,” said Mykhailo Semikin, head of Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration.
He said rescuers were continuing their search for people under the rubble.
An AFP correspondent at the scene saw people being pulled from the rubble by Ukrainian emergency services.
“We saw people under the rubble -- a woman, her husband and a child,” one volunteer rescuer, Daniil Pishkin, told AFP.
He added that he saw two people rescued from the wreckage but “unfortunately there was a little girl who died.”
A resident of one of the buildings that was hit, who identified herself as Iryna, 69, said she just had time to seek refuge in the toilets after receiving an air raid warning.
She said her two neighbors were killed.
“They were 75 years old. They were simply thrown out there, onto the street. They didn’t make it to the hospital,” she told AFP.
The Zaporizhzhia region, located just a few dozen kilometers from the front line, and its capital by the same name have been the target of frequent strikes.
Russia has intensified its strikes on Ukrainian territory in recent months, causing a growing number of civilian casualties.
Diplomatic efforts mediated by the United States to end the war more than four years since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine have so far yielded no results.

item.title: Yemen govt forces say advancing against Houthis around key waterway
item.description:
Yemeni military sources told AFP on Saturday their forces were advancing against the Houthis in areas around the Bab al-Mandab strait but have not yet secured control of the waterway, after the government launched an operation to capture lost territory.
The Saudi-backed government last week announced a counter-offensive aimed at retaking all areas held by the Houthis, after the pro-Iran group seized Yemen’s entire western coastline in a lightning offensive.
The Houthis confirmed that government forces had attacked in the Bab al-Mandab area but they claimed to have repelled the assault.
“Saudi-led forces attempted to advance from the Ras al-Ara area in Lahj governorate towards the area south of Bab al-Mandab,” Hizam al-Asad, a member of the Houthis’ political bureau, told AFP.
“However, our forces repelled them outside the Bab al-Mandab zone, inflicting heavy losses in personnel and equipment and forcing the survivors to retreat.
“Our forces maintain control over Bab al-Mandab, Mayun Island, and the remaining areas along the country’s western coast,” he said.
Sources from the military of Yemen’s internationally recognized government also said Mayun Island -- located in the heart of the strait -- remained in Houthi hands as fighting continued.
Claims by the warring parties have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast on the ground and access for journalists difficult.
Clashes in western Yemen, specifically around the strait, had killed at least 63 people in the past 24 hours, military sources from both sides told AFP on Saturday.
Thirty-five members of government forces had been killed, while 28 Houthis had died, the sources said.
On Friday a Yemeni military source confirmed to AFP that their forces had launched a “major operation” in the strait region, supported by air power from Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen’s government.
After four years of relative calm, Yemen’s civil war reignited in July before the Houthi gains on Yemen’s western coastline.
Saudi Arabia leads an international military coalition helping the Yemeni government fight the Houthis.
Early on Saturday the coalition said it had destroyed more than 130 Houthi targets in a “large-scale operation.”
The Houthis’ Al-Masirah TV channel reported on Saturday that enemy strikes had targeted the Bab al-Mandab area.
It also reported four Saudi strikes on the capital Sanaa’s international airport on Saturday, a day after saying two were killed in a Saudi strike on the airport.
In addition to battling Yemeni government forces on the ground, the Houthis have also been firing on targets inside Saudi Arabia, attacking transport hubs, oil facilities and other civilian sites with drones and missiles.
Riyadh said Friday that attacks on the Saudi capital’s international airport had killed three people the previous day.
Saudi Arabia has been retaliating with strikes on key Houthi targets inside Yemen. Houthi media reported on Friday that two people had died in attacks on the airport in the Houthi-controlled capital Sanaa.
Ordinary civilians have been paying the price for the renewed fighting in one of the world’s poorest countries, with more than 200,000 people displaced since July, according to UN data.

item.title: Turkiye social media ban for under-15s takes effect Nov 1
item.description:
Turkiye on Saturday formally declared a ban on the use of social media for under-15s, scheduled to come into effect on November 1.
It has joined a growing number of countries legislating to protect children and teenagers from the harmful effects of online platforms.
The official state journal published the decision following the adoption of a law by parliament in April.
It stipulates that social media providers must “take the necessary technical and administrative measures, including age verification, to implement” protections for young people.
“No service likely to produce an addictive effect in children may be offered.”
Countries including Australia have introduced restrictions on social media for children and others such as Britain and France are pushing to do the same.
They aim to protect children from digital risks such as screen addiction, lack of sleep, bullying and eating disorders.
Rights groups have complained of restrictions on freedom of expression in Turkiye targeting LGBTQ communities, the media and the political opposition. Numerous social media accounts have been blocked in recent weeks.

item.title: Rizvi: Khaleda Zia, Tarique Rahman laid groundwork for July uprising
item.description:
BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi Ahmed has said former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman laid the groundwork for the July uprising of 2024.
He made the remarks at a memorial meeting organized by the Shaheed Jehad Smriti Parishad at the National Press Club in Dhaka on Saturday, marking the 36th death anniversary of Nazir Uddin Jehad, a student leader killed during the anti-autocracy movement in 1990.
Speaking as the chief guest, Rizvi said Jehad had traveled from Sirajganj to participate in the movement against then military ruler HM Ershad and sacrificed his life for the cause.
He said Jehad’s sacrifice, alongside 9 years of sustained protests and resistance, contributed to the fall of Ershad’s autocratic regime and helped strengthen the movement for the restoration of democracy.
“The July uprising of 2024 did not emerge in a single day,” Rizvi said, adding that it was the culmination of a prolonged struggle against what he described as authoritarian rule.
Rizvi said Khaleda Zia had maintained her uncompromising stance despite facing what he alleged were false cases, physical torture and imprisonment over the years. Tarique Rahman, meanwhile, continued to lead the movement from abroad, he added.
According to Rizvi, the struggles led by the 2 BNP leaders helped create the conditions that ultimately led to the July uprising.
Criticizing the previous government, Rizvi alleged that the forces defeated in the 1990 anti-autocracy movement and those ousted in 2024 were linked by a common political legacy.
He accused the previous government of presiding over widespread corruption, the looting of public resources, the depletion of bank funds and the laundering of thousands of crores of taka abroad during its 17-year rule. He also alleged that enforced disappearances and killings had been used to suppress political opposition.
Rizvi claimed that supporters of the previous regime remained embedded at different levels of the administration and society.
He urged the government to identify corrupt officials and those allegedly involved in abuses under the previous administration and take strict action against them.
“There should be no leniency towards those who carried out crossfire killings, killed people and plundered public money,” he said, adding that the public would support the government if it took firm action against wrongdoing.
Turning to the upcoming Durga Puja celebrations, Rizvi said Bangladesh had a long tradition of communal harmony, with people of different faiths participating in one another’s religious festivals.
However, he expressed concern that forces opposed to the current political order might attempt to create unrest around the festival.
He called on BNP leaders and activists, as well as members of the public, to remain vigilant and help protect Puja mandaps to ensure that members of the Hindu community could celebrate the festival peacefully and without fear.
The meeting was chaired by BNP Standing Committee member Amanullah Aman, president of the Shaheed Jehad Smriti Parishad. Former Dhaka University Central Students’ Union general secretary Khairul Kabir Khokon and former assistant general secretary Nazim Uddin Alam jointly moderated the event.
Among those who addressed the meeting were 1990 Students’ Struggle Council president Md Mustafizur Rahman Babul, BNP Chairperson’s Advisory Council member Habibur Rahman Habib, former Begum Rokeya Hall vice-president and MP Shirin Sultana, former Dhaka College vice-president and BNP volunteer affairs secretary Mir Sarafat Ali Sapu, and former Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal general secretary Saif Mahmud Jewel.

Mahdi Amin: Govt plans support for students failing SSC exams
item.description:
Prime Minister's Adviser for Education and Primary and Mass Education Mahdi Amin on Saturday said the government is formulating a permanent action plan to support students who fail to achieve expected results or are unsuccessful in the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examinations. Under the directive of the prime minister, the plan will include technical training, language education, seed funding for small businesses and if necessary, an opportunity to retake failed subjects within three months, he said.
Mahdi Amin made the remarks while addressing the "Challenged Students Convention 2026" as the chief guest at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in Agargaon.
Campaign for Popular Education (CAMPE) and Plan International Bangladesh jointly organized the convention, chaired by CAMPE Executive Director Rasheda K Chowdhury.
Mahdi Amin said around 0.69 million students had failed to achieve their expected results in this year's SSC examinations, stressing that academic performance should not determine their future.
He said students interested in technical and vocational education would be connected with local Technical Training Centres (TTCs), while those with promising business or innovative ideas could receive seed funding to start small businesses.
Short-term language courses lasting three to six months in Japanese, Korean, Chinese and European languages would also be introduced to help skilled workers explore international employment opportunities, he added.
Regarding the proposal to allow students to retake failed subjects within three months instead of waiting a year, Mahdi Amin said the government was considering it positively and hoped that changes would be introduced soon.
He said poor examination results could stem from various factors, including financial hardship, teacher shortages, inadequate classrooms and family problems. The government was working to address these challenges, he added.
"Life cannot be judged on the basis of certificates. Performing poorly in one subject does not diminish anyone's talent or creativity," he said.

The physics, economics, and market reality of curved monitors
item.description:
For 70 years, the display industry had one engineering religion: flatness.
When LCD panels took over from cathode ‑ ray tubes in the early 2000s, they quietly ended the era of curved screens—a shape dictated not by design, but by the physics of vacuum ‑ tube displays.
The industry declared victory. The perfectly flat screen became the baseline, then the standard, then the commodity.
Then, roughly a decade ago, the industry decided to curve the screens again.
This change is not about following trends or marketing strategies. It is an acknowledgment that for seven decades, the display was optimized for itself rather than for the person in front of it.
The ASUS ROG Swift OLED PG39WCDM, a 39-inch 800R curved OLED ultrawide, is the most aggressive commercial example of this contradiction today. (I owe thanks to Global Brand PLC, the authorized ASUS distributor in Bangladesh for providing this review unit, though the analysis remains strictly independent.)
Now, here is how this contradiction plays out in real life: imagine spending eight hours staring at a big, flat screen. Your eyes are not stationary.
They are constantly moving across the screen, from the code editor to the browser, from the data dashboard to the chat window. Each sweep asks your neck to turn.
Occupational health research consistently documents that if you look sideways beyond 35 degrees from the center, your neck muscles experience measurable strain over time.
The screen does not cause you pain right away. It just accumulates the debt silently.
The 800R curve exists to cancel that debt. Everything that follows is an honest accounting of whether it works, and what it costs to try.
Why the industry finally bent
The “R” in 800R stands for radius, measured in millimeters. The math works inversely: the smaller the number, the tighter the curve.
The 1800R gives a gentle curve, while 1000R is often described as “matching the human visual field”— a marketing term that is approximately, but not precisely, true.
The distinction between 1000R and 800R is categorical.
At 1000R, the curve feels natural for your eyes. It stops penalizing you for sitting close to a wide screen, but that is about it. At 800R, the design actively assists you.
When you sit exactly 80 centimeters from the panel, every pixel, from the dead center to the far corners, is at the exact same optical distance from your eyes.
The edges stop behaving as periphery. They become present. Your eyes stop wandering and start focusing.
The panel stops feeling like a wide wall you have to move around to see everything, and it starts acting like a concave cockpit: every window, tool, and file is within natural visual reach without you having to turn.
That is the whole reason the 800R design is the most effective.
So, where is the catch?
The selfish display
The 800R curve is the most focused single-user piece of display technology the consumer market has ever produced.
By optimizing every pixel for one viewer at the dead center of the curve, it actively degrades the experience for anyone else.
A colleague standing next to you sees distorted geometry: the far edge appears pinched, and straight lines bend.
This is precisely why curved televisions failed commercially in living rooms a decade ago. The engineering is structurally hostile to shared viewing.
The limit is absolute. If your workday involves frequent side-by-side collaboration, this monitor answers the wrong question entirely, regardless of its other credentials. Stop here.
But for the single-user command center focused on tasks like coding, data analysis, video editing, or gaming, this structural challenge becomes a benefit.
The design that might bother a second viewer is the same design that helps the first person concentrate. The display acts as a boundary that worth something real.
The limitation is not a flaw.
The hidden tax
The PG39WCDM's packaging is the first honest signal of what you are getting. The box is enormous, but the display inside is not.
Once the 800R arc wraps those 39 inches around your peripheral vision, the horizontal footprint is comparable to a standard 34-inch flat panel. The curvature makes it feel compact.
The depth is not.
A tightly curved display needs strong structural stability.
The stand of the display takes up more than 30 centimeters of desk depth.
On a standard 120-centimeter desk, that pushes the keyboard to the edge and takes away the little extra space most people use unconsciously.
The obvious solution is a VESA monitor arm. But the 800R curvature makes this more expensive than it appears.
The panel's center of gravity is closer to the mount than a regular arm accounts for.
A heavy-duty arm that can handle the weight costs approximately BDT 8,000 additionally.
You have to include it in your total cost of ownership calculation.
The text clarity problem
The display uses a 3440x1440 WOLED panel covering 39 diagonal inches.
The pixel density lands at approximately 96 PPI, below the 110 PPI threshold that Windows has historically treated as the baseline for comfortable text rendering.
The WOLED subpixel structure compounds the concern, as the panel uses a red, white, blue, and green layout.
Windows ClearType rendering assumes standard RGB.
Sub-100 PPI plus non-standard subpixels is a formula for visible fringing: the kind that makes fine text in spreadsheets and code editors uncomfortable to read for long periods.
However, in practice, at 80 centimeters, with ASUS’s Clear Pixel Edge algorithm running, the fringing is not noticeable under normal use.
But you can spot it if you move close to the panel and consciously look for it.
The WOLED trade-off is real, but it is almost completely invisible at the viewing distance the display was engineered for. The fear is understandable, but the actual practice is not the issue.
The color performance closes a gap that mattered more two years ago.
The display offers factory calibration, VESA-certified True Black levels, and 99% DCI-P3 coverage, along with a 240Hz refresh rate and 0.03ms instantaneous response time.
Color-critical studio work still belongs on a specialized ProArt display. Everything adjacent to it belongs here.
The Economics
The Tk230,000 price tag demands a real economic justification, not just a list of features. It needs a comparison.
The honest alternative is not a cheaper curved monitor.
It is a dual-panel configuration: two high-quality 27-inch 1440p IPS monitors at Tk60,000 each, a dual-monitor arm at Tk10,000, and remaining Tk100,000 for storage, peripherals, a sound system, or a laptop upgrade.
That is a setup a serious user would genuinely consider at the same budget.
The case for the PG39WCDM against that alternative rests on three specific claims.
First, a single-panel workspace eliminates the dead zone between two monitors where windows get lost and the cursor breaks continuity.
Second, no IPS panel, no matter the cost, matches an OLED substrate for True Black, response time, or maintaining color accuracy for long periods, which is critical for anyone doing creative and productivity work from the same desk.
Third, OLED panel costs are dropping faster than IPS premiums are rising. Buying before the price compresses is the wrong framing; buying at the leading edge of mass adoption has historically been the smart move.
The market backs up that third claim.
TrendForce Q2 2026 data shows that ASUS is leading the global OLED monitor market with a 23.1% share.
Market Intelo estimates the global curved monitor market at $5.8 billion in 2025, projecting growth to $9.6 billion by 2034 at a 6.8% CAGR.
Asia-Pacific commands 38.5% of that revenue and is the fastest-growing region. Bangladesh is definitely part of that growth, not just watching from the sidelines.
ASUS is not a brand making a bet on curved OLED. They are the brand that emerged victorious in the first round of a market that is still in its infancy.
Verdict
The debate between curved and flat is framed as a battle where one technology must eventually defeat the other. That framing is wrong, and it produces the wrong verdict.
The correct question is: what problem are you actually trying to solve?
Flat displays solve a universal problem well: a stable, shared, glare-manageable display surface for the widest range of users and configurations.
Curved displays, on the other hand, solve a specific problem better.
That problem belongs to a specific user, at a specific focal distance, in a specific working posture, doing a specific category of work.
The PG39WCDM is a machine built for one person, doing focused solo work, at 80 centimeters, for eight or more hours a day.
Every engineering decision on this panel, from the 800R arc and OLED substrate to the 240Hz refresh rate and factory calibration, is optimized for that exact configuration.
Deviate from it, and you pay a measurable cost. Stay inside it, and you get the best single-panel productivity and performance display currently available at a reasonable price.
If you are a solo operator, the curve is not just a visual preference; it is a structural decision about how you work.
And for everyone else, the flat screen is still the right answer. Not a compromise. An honest answer to a different question.
The writer is a contributor and tech enthusiast

Dengue: Four more die, 1,935 hospitalized in 24 hours
item.description:
Four people died of dengue, and 1,631 were hospitalized with the Aedes mosquito-borne disease in the last 24 hours till 8am on Saturday, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
With this development, the country has recorded 299 deaths from dengue this year.
Of the new dengue cases, 703 were recorded in Dhaka division, 61 in Mymensingh division, 234 in Chittagong division, 184 in Khulna division, 141 in Rajshahi division, 75 in Rangpur division, 219 in Barisal division and 14 in Sylhet division.
A total of 97,082 dengue patients have so far been hospitalized across the country this year, according to the DGHS report.
However, in the last 24 hours, 1,627 patients recovered and were discharged from hospitals.
So far, 91,007 dengue patients have recovered and returned home after receiving treatment this year.
A total of 102,861 people were infected with dengue, and 413 people died from the disease last year.

item.title: Bangladesh discusses €250 million loan for women's health initiative
item.description:
Bangladesh discussed a proposed €250 million loan from the European Investment Bank (EIB) to implement a women's health initiative with international development partners during the World Health Summit (WHS) 2026 in Berlin, Germany, on Saturday.
The bilateral and technical discussions took place at the Charité campus in Berlin, involving a high-level delegation from the Bangladesh government and international development partners.
The Bangladesh delegation was led by Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain and Special Assistant to the Prime Minister on Health Ziauddin Hyder.
The proposed Women's Health Initiative aims to reduce maternal mortality, ensure early detection of cervical and breast cancers, and develop modern facilities to provide round-the-clock emergency obstetric services at the union level.
The discussions also covered strengthening district hospitals and introducing a digital patient-tracking system.
The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin, and the Berlin Institute of Health (BIH) are providing technical and strategic support for the initiative.
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain said: “This international partnership will play an important role in ensuring quality healthcare for women and girls in remote areas of Bangladesh.”
The Bangladesh delegation also visited Charité Hospital in Berlin to observe its medical facilities and cancer screening services.
The parties agreed to form a joint working group to support the future development of healthcare systems in both countries.

item.title: Abdul Awal Mintoo: Bangladesh, India to hold talks on elephant corridor in Sherpur
item.description:
Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo on Saturday said the government would soon initiate talks with India under an existing protocol to establish a cross-border corridor for wild elephants roaming the Garo Hills in Sherpur.
Around 130 to 135 wild elephants that came from India's Meghalaya have become stranded in the Garo Hills of Sherpur as border fencing has prevented them from returning to their habitat, he said.
The minister said the government would request the Indian authorities to open gates in the fencing to allow the elephants to return, although previous requests had not received a positive response.
At the same time, initiatives would be taken to develop forest areas in Sherpur into safe habitats for the elephants, he added.
The minister made the remarks while speaking at a discussion on resolving human-elephant conflict and conserving wild elephants at Madhutila Eco Park in Nalitabari upazila of Sherpur.
He said the scenic Garo Hills, its wild elephants and the surrounding natural environment would be used to develop the area into a tourism hub. This would create economic opportunities for local people while helping protect elephants and reduce human-elephant conflict, he added.
The Sherpur district administration and the Mymensingh Forest Division organized the discussion with lawmakers from elephant-affected areas, Elephant Response Team (ERT) members, journalists and volunteers involved in elephant conservation. Deputy Commissioner Farida Yesmin chaired the event.
Sherpur-2 lawmaker Engineer Fahim Chowdhury, Chief Conservator of Forests Md Amir Hossain Chowdhury, Conservator of Forests for the Wildlife and Nature Conservation Region Md Sanaullah Patwari, Central Region Conservator of Forests ASM Zahir Uddin Akon, Mymensingh Divisional Forest Officer Kazi Muhammad Nurul Karim and Police Superintendent AKM Johirul Islam spoke as special guests.

item.title: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee detained by Delhi Police; CJP demands release
item.description:
YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was detained by Delhi Police at his residence in Gurugram’s Sector 56 on Saturday ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) planned protest at Jantar Mantar, NDTV reported, citing police sources.
Rathee had arrived to join the demonstration, prompting heightened security arrangements across the national capital.
According to sources, around 50 Delhi Police personnel arrived at Rathee’s Gurugram residence on Saturday morning and detained him.
The detention drew a sharp response from the CJP, which demanded his “immediate release”.
On Friday evening, Rathee announced his participation in Saturday’s protest in a video posted on his X account.
A vocal critic of the Narendra Modi government, Rathee arrived in India from Germany earlier this week and joined a CJP protest in Bengaluru on October 8.
Rathee has a substantial online following, with 19.2 million Instagram followers, 3.3 million on X, and 33 million YouTube subscribers.
Earlier this week, Delhi Police denied permission for the protest, citing security concerns and procedural requirements.
Police have stepped up preventive detentions and deployed personnel at strategic locations to prevent protesters from reaching the protest site.
More than 400 people were detained overnight, while hundreds of trains were cancelled and dozens of metro stations shut ahead of a large-scale protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in central Delhi on Saturday.
The CJP mobilised supporters to gather at Jantar Mantar, while the Centre deployed more than 20,000 police and Central Armed Police Forces personnel to maintain law and order.

item.title: Tagore mural targeted outside Shilpakala Academy, one detained
item.description:
Police detained ANM Ayas, a leader of Rashtra Sanglap Forum, on Saturday afternoon for allegedly attempting to deface a mural of Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore outside Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy in the capital’s Segunbagicha area.
The incident occurred just five days after Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) cleared the footpath of encroachments and decorated an adjoining wall with portraits of 10 prominent figures from Bengali literature, art and culture.
Shahbag Police Station Sub-Inspector Abdul Khalek confirmed the detention, saying Ayas had been taken to the police station after attempting to erase Tagore’s portrait.
The incident comes amid criticism over the selection of cultural personalities featured in the murals, particularly the inclusion of figures from West Bengal and the absence of women.
According to reports, police intervened after an attempt was made to apply black or white paint to the portraits outside the academy.
The Daily Campus reported that three people, including Ayas, were detained in connection with the incident. Other reports initially confirmed only Ayas’s detention.
The Daily Campus also described Ayas as president of Rashtra Sanglap Forum, while other outlets identified him as its member secretary.
On October 5, DSCC reopened the Segunbagicha footpath following an operation to remove encroachments.
As part of the renovation, portraits of 10 cultural figures were painted on a roadside wall near Shilpakala Academy.
They included Rabindranath Tagore, national poet Kazi Nazrul Islam, Shilpacharya Zainul Abedin, filmmaker Satyajit Ray, philosopher and social reformer Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, Fakir Lalon Shah, artist SM Sultan, filmmaker Zahir Raihan, folk singer Shah Abdul Karim and actor Humayun Faridi.
The project also included new dustbins, benches for pedestrians and repairs to the boundary wall.
The newly renovated stretch was opened to pedestrians after the removal of makeshift shops and other obstructions.
It was not immediately clear whether any formal case had been filed or what further legal action police intended to take.

item.title: PM assures support for waste-to-fuel technology
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Saturday assured support for a technology that could turn waste into fuel oil and help reduce Bangladesh’s dependence on imported energy.
He gave the assurance as a team of researchers led by Khulna University of Engineering and Technology (Kuet) Professor Dr Md Khalequzzaman briefed him on the technology at his office in Tejgaon, said a release issued by the PM’s Press Wing.
The technology uses a process known as hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) to convert human waste, waste from sewage treatment plants, kitchen waste and agricultural residues into fuel oil.
The researchers said they have been working on the technology for around 10 years and have achieved a 50–55% biocrude yield in laboratory tests. They have also made progress in producing biocrude with a high diesel content.
The next step is to set up a pilot plant capable of processing one to three tons of waste daily to assess the technology’s efficiency, production costs and commercial viability. The estimated cost of the pilot project is Tk100–120 crore.
According to the researchers, the technology, if developed for commercial-scale production, could replace around 10–15% of imported crude oil and save foreign currency equivalent to Tk6,500–13,000 crore annually.
However, the estimates would need to be validated through large-scale technical and economic assessments, they said.
The researchers said the technology could also help reduce environmental pollution, improve waste management and create opportunities for developing a domestic fuel industry.
The Prime Minister assured them of the government’s necessary cooperation in advancing the initiative.
Power and Energy Minister Iqbal Mahmood Tuku, State Minister Anindya Islam Amit, University Grants Commission member Professor Abdullah Al Mamun, Kuet Vice-Chancellor Professor Mohammad Masud and Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation Chairman Dr Mohammad Rafiqul Islam were present at the briefing.

item.title: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, two others detained aboard plane in Delhi
item.description:
Police detained Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijit Dipke and two other party members aboard an aircraft shortly after it landed at Delhi Airport, ahead of the party’s planned protest at Jantar Mantar, reports NDTV.
Dipke went live on Instagram as police entered the aircraft. The video shows officers detaining Dipke, Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka inside the plane.

item.title: States told by Indian govt to stop protest march to Delhi
item.description:
India’s Union Ministry of Home Affairs has asked all states and Union Territories to coordinate with Delhi Police and take preventive measures to stop protesters from travelling to the national capital ahead of a planned demonstration by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), The Hindu reported.
In a letter to state chief secretaries and police chiefs on Friday, Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan flagged the “grave law and order and public order implications” of the planned protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday.
The protesters are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over concerns about the Election Commission’s functioning and its handling of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Authorities have introduced sweeping restrictions ahead of the demonstration. These include preventive detentions, train cancellations, the closure of metro stations and the suspension of mobile internet services in parts of central Delhi.
The restrictions have drawn criticism from protest organisers, who have described the measures as intimidation by the authorities.
In its letter, the Union government said Delhi Police had rejected the organisers’ request to hold the demonstration at Jantar Mantar, ANI reported.
The ministry also cited what it described as a “documented history of non-compliance with lawful directions” by the CJP and organisations supporting it during an earlier protest. It alleged that the previous demonstration, involving participants from several states, had disrupted public order and damaged public property, The Hindu reported.
The ministry said intelligence inputs suggested that CJP members and supporters planned to defy prohibitory orders and enter Delhi through multiple routes.
It directed states and Union Territories to “immediately operationalise preventive measures” in coordination with Delhi Police to maintain public order and protect critical infrastructure.
The government also stressed the need for real-time intelligence sharing among state agencies, transit authorities and Delhi Police to ensure coordinated action.
The planned demonstration follows several days of protests by opposition INDIA bloc members in Delhi and other parts of India, calling for Kumar’s resignation over concerns about electoral roll revisions and the functioning of the Election Commission.

item.title: Mahatma Gandhi’s great-grandson detained in Mumbai ahead of CJP protest
item.description:
Mumbai Police detained Tushar Gandhi, great-grandson of Mahatma Gandhi and president of Hum Bharat Ke Log, along with his associates on Saturday as they headed to August Kranti Maidan for a protest in support of the Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) demonstration in Delhi, The Indian Express reported.
The protest was scheduled for 3:30pm.
A police official said Gandhi was picked up from Bandra and taken to DN Nagar police station. Gandhi claimed on X that he had been arrested and taken to an unknown location. Police denied arresting him, saying he had only been detained.
Guddi S L, vice-president of the organisation, was picked up from Andheri and taken to MIDC police station, police confirmed.
On Friday, Gandhi posted a poster on X urging Mumbaikars to join him at August Kranti Maidan, the site from which the Quit India movement was launched in 1942. The protest was planned in support of the CJP’s demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
Gamdevi Police said no application had been received or permission granted for the demonstration.
“Due to a Supreme Court ruling, the Mumbai police cannot grant permission to hold a protest at August Kranti Maidan as the land belongs to the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). No one had approached us in the first instance,” a senior police official said on Friday.
Guddi disputed the claim, saying she had emailed police seeking permission because Gandhi was not in the city but had received no response.
“Gandhi has been called by the police, and they are telling him not to protest. They have also asked him about his location and said that they would detain him,” she said on Friday.
The detentions come amid heightened police vigilance across Maharashtra ahead of the CJP’s planned protest at Jantar Mantar. Police in Mumbai and other parts of the state have been monitoring people suspected of planning to travel to Delhi.
Mumbai Police detained more than 200 people on Friday to prevent them from travelling to the national capital, the report said.

item.title: Two crude bombs hurled outside PM’s Office, police seek suspects
item.description:
Two crude bombs, were hurled outside the Prime Minister’s Office in Tejgaon, Dhaka, early Saturday, prompting police to launch an investigation to identify and arrest those involved.
The incident occurred around 1:15am. One of the bombs exploded, while the other was safely detonated in a controlled explosion by the Bomb Disposal Unit of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s (DMP) Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit.
DMP Tejgaon Division Deputy Commissioner Ibne Mizan said police were working to identify and arrest the two suspects who arrived on a motorcycle.
According to him, the two men reached the area around 1:15am, surveyed their surroundings for two to three minutes, hurled the bombs and fled. Police received information that they headed towards Kafrul via Agargaon.
Ibne Mizan said police teams began investigating immediately after the incident. Footage from nearby CCTV cameras has been collected to help identify the suspects, and the incident is being treated as a priority.

item.title: Job seekers block roads in Dhaka over youth development exam paper leak
item.description:
Job seekers blocked several major roads in Dhaka on Saturday to protest the alleged leak of question papers for the Department of Youth Development’s recruitment examination, disrupting traffic in several areas.
Around noon, protesters blocked the road in front of Mirpur Bangla College near the Technical intersection.
Job seekers also took to the streets in Motijheel and at the Aarong intersection in Asad Gate, bringing traffic to a standstill in the affected areas.
The protesters questioned why question paper leaks were still occurring under the current government, recalling that such incidents had also taken place under the previous regime. They questioned the significance of the July 2024 uprising, in which thousands of people sacrificed their lives.
They demanded that the government identify those responsible and ensure exemplary punishment, as well as take strict measures to prevent similar incidents in the future.
Afzal Hossain, a job seeker, said he had travelled hundreds of kilometres from a remote area to Dhaka to sit for the examination.
“After enduring so much hardship to reach the exam centre, I learned that the examination had been postponed because the question paper had been leaked,” he said.
“Who will compensate the thousands of us who went to such lengths to sit for the examination? We demand exemplary punishment for everyone involved in the question paper leak,” he added.

item.title: Humaiun: Bangladesh views Makkah Defence Agreement positively
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Saturday said Bangladesh was positively considering the Makkah Defence Agreement, with any decision to be guided by national interests and the potential contribution of the country's peacekeeping expertise to regional peace and stability.
“We are having positive discussions on the Makkah Defence Agreement. We are viewing it positively,” he said while addressing a national seminar at the Foreign Service Academy in the capital.
Kobir said Bangladesh could take a favourable decision if the agreement served its national interests and its peacekeeping expertise could contribute to the welfare of Muslim nations and help maintain peace and stability in the Middle East.
“If it falls within the national interests of Bangladesh and converges, and we feel that our peacekeeping expertise can add value in serving Muslim nations and keeping a stable, peaceful Middle East, then there is every scope to take a positive decision on the matter,” he said.
The Bangladesh Institute of International and Strategic Studies (BIISS) and the Center for Migration Studies of North South University (NSU) jointly organised the seminar titled “From Workforce to Strategic Partnership: Reimagining Bangladesh-KSA Relations.”
The state minister also said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had accepted an invitation from Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince to visit the Kingdom.
“He has accepted and will do so at some point very soon,” Kobir said.
He said the Crown Prince had also expressed interest in visiting Bangladesh, adding that Dhaka would welcome him at a mutually convenient time.
Kobir said the proposed visits reflected growing political ties between the two countries. He also described Bangladesh as a strong partner of Saudi Arabia in maritime security.
Calling for a comprehensive economic and strategic partnership, he said bilateral relations should expand beyond their traditional focus on labour migration and remittances.
“While that foundation remains important, it cannot be the ceiling of our ambition,” he said.
He said Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 and Bangladesh's economic transformation had created common interests in investment, human capital, technology and connectivity.
Discussions were underway on a possible investment fund to facilitate joint investments and partnerships in priority sectors, he added.
The state minister identified renewable energy, infrastructure, ports, logistics, agriculture, fisheries, food security, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, information technology and artificial intelligence as promising areas for Saudi investment.
He said such investments required a predictable and transparent business environment, improved institutional coordination and timely decision-making.
Kobir stressed the need to shift towards trained and certified professionals to meet the changing demands of Saudi Arabia's labour market.
He called for stronger cooperation among training institutions, universities and industries to ensure skills certification aligned with Saudi market requirements.
The welfare, dignity and rights of Bangladeshi workers in Saudi Arabia would remain a government priority, he said.
Kobir also highlighted opportunities for knowledge and technology partnerships, alongside cooperation in ports, shipping, logistics, aviation and supply chains.
“The next chapter of Bangladesh-Saudi Arabia relations should therefore be defined by value creation rather than volume alone,” he said.
Saudi Arabia’s Ambassador to Bangladesh Dr Abdullah Zafer bin Abiyah addressed the seminar as the guest of honour. Foreign Ministry Secretary (Bilateral) Dr Md Nazrul Islam and Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Secretary Md Mokhtar Ahmed spoke as special guests.
BIISS Director General Major General A S M Ridwanur Rahman and NSU Vice-Chancellor Professor Abdul Hannan Chowdhury also addressed the seminar.
Speaking to journalists after the event, Kobir reiterated that peace and stability in the Middle East and the Muslim world were central to Bangladesh's consideration of the Makkah Defence Agreement.
He said maintaining peace in the region encompassing Makkah and Madinah was a key objective, adding that Bangladesh could deploy its peacekeeping expertise more effectively and extensively across the world.
He said initiatives regarding participation in the agreement or association with the alliance were being considered positively, with regional peace and stability remaining the priority.
Kobir said regular high-level exchanges, including ministerial and official visits in both directions, were strengthening bilateral engagement.
He also stressed the need to diversify employment opportunities into energy, technology and other promising sectors while sending more highly skilled professionals to Saudi Arabia.
“We are also holding very positive discussions with Saudi Arabia and, God willing, many new opportunities will emerge between the two countries,” he said.
The state minister said there was scope for a broad investment partnership under which Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia could jointly invest in profitable sectors.
“The days of dependency are over. We are now placing emphasis on an equal partnership between the two countries and on sustainable policies,” he told journalists.

item.title: Durga Puja festivities begin with observance of Mahalaya
item.description:
Mahalaya, which marks the beginning of Hindu community’s largest religious festival Durga Puja, is being observed across the country amid festivity on Saturday.
From early morning, temples across the country resonated with Chandipath, tarpan rituals, and devotional hymns in praise of Goddess Durga.
The serene autumn dawn ushered in Devipaksha, the fortnight dedicated to the goddess, through the traditional recitation of sacred verses.
Mahalaya that is considered as ceremonial invocation of goddess Durga is observed seven days prior to the initiation of the Durga Puja, the largest religious festival of the Hindu community.
Hindus believe the earth prepares itself and welcomes the coming of the Goddess and her children, through the celebration.
On this day, Hindus remember and pay homage to the deceased ancestors by performing a puja, and offering Brahmins clothes, food and sweets in their name.
From this day, the countdown to Durga Puja begins.
This year, Shashthi Puja will be celebrated on October 17 while Bijoya Dashami on October 21 will mark the goddess’s departure to Kailash.
Scriptures mention three major milestones of Durga Puja—Mahalaya, Bodhon, and Sandhi Puja. On Mahalaya, Goddess Durga receives the divine mandate to defeat the demon king Mahishasura.
Empowered by the combined forces of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva, she emerges as `Mahashakti’, adorned with ten weapons and riding a lion, ultimately slaying Mahishasura after a nine-day battle.

Brazil’s Lula scraps gasoline tax ahead of runoff election
item.description:
Brazil’s government announced on Friday that gasoline taxes will be temporarily scrapped, two weeks ahead of the runoff election between incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro.
Lula, who is seeking his fourth term, is trying to contain rising fuel prices amid a global spike in oil prices driven by the war in the Middle East.
The gasoline tax, which was set at 0.89 reais ($0.18) per liter, would be waived for 30 days, according to the government.
The measure announced on Friday also expands subsidies for importers of diesel, the predominant fuel used in Brazil’s freight transport.
“The objective is to ensure that imports remain viable at a critical moment for supply,” the presidency said in a statement.
The fiscal impact of the tax exemptions will be offset by Brazil’s “extraordinary revenues” from oil exports, it said.
The runoff election on October 25 was set after Lula won 45% of the vote in the first round and Bolsonaro received 47%.
Bolsonaro called his opponent “irresponsible,” warning that Lula was placing a “bomb” on consumers’ laps and that diesel prices could rise after the election.
Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro, repeatedly criticized the government during his campaign for failing to control the cost of living.
Inflation in Brazil rose by 0.82% in September, the statistics authority said on Friday.

Barrister Abdul Muntaquim Chaudhury dies at 97
item.description:
Barrister Abdul Muntaquim Chaudhury, a Bangladeshi politician, lawyer and organizer of the Liberation War, died in Melbourne, Australia, on October 9, 2026. He was 97.
Born on September 2, 1929, Chaudhury served as a member of Pakistan’s National Assembly in the 1960s and was re-elected in 1970. After Bangladesh gained independence, he became a member of the Constituent Assembly and helped draft the country’s constitution.
In 1973, he was appointed Bangladesh’s ambassador to Japan. He later served as the country’s ambassador to the German Democratic Republic.
After returning to Bangladesh in 1979, Chaudhury became the founding executive director of the Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust (Blast).
Abu Taher Abdul Muntaquim Chaudhury, whose family descended from the Kanihati Chaudhury family of Sylhet, was the youngest child of Khan Bahadur Tazzammul Ali Chaudhury.
He completed his Intermediate of Arts (IA) at Aligarh Muslim University before studying at Santiniketan and St Xavier’s College. He earned his bachelor’s degree from the University of Calcutta and was later called to the bar at Lincoln’s Inn in London.

Dhaka’s air quality 4th worst in the world Saturday morning
item.description:
Dhaka, the overcrowded capital city of Bangladesh, has ranked 4th on the list of cities with the worst air quality, with an AQI index of 181 at 9:06am on Saturday.
Dhaka’s air was classified as "unhealthy", according to the air quality and pollution city ranking.
Singapore, Malaysia’s Kuala Lumpur and India's Kolkata occupied the first, second and third spots in the list, with AQI scores of 200, 198 and 192, respectively.
When the AQI value for particle pollution is between 101 and 150, air quality is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", between 150 and 200 is "unhealthy", between 201 and 300 is said to be "very unhealthy", while a reading of 301+ is considered "hazardous", posing serious health risks to residents.
The AQI, an index for reporting daily air quality, informs people how clean or polluted the air of a certain city is and what associated health effects might be a concern for them.
The AQI in Bangladesh is based on five pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), NO2, CO, SO2, and ozone.
Dhaka has long been grappling with air pollution issues. Its air quality usually turns unhealthy in winter and improves during the monsoon.

Police Additional DIG Tutul Chakraborty dismissed from service
item.description:
The government has dismissed Additional Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of Police Tutul Chakraborty from service after finding him guilty of misconduct, including leaving his post ahead of schedule and using an airport VIP lounge while identifying himself as a “DIG.”
The decision was announced in a notification issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs on Wednesday. According to the notification, Chakraborty was attached to the office of the Rajshahi Range DIG while under suspension and had been “absconding” since January 23.
The notification said Chakraborty had been granted 2 days of leave with permission on November 14 and 15, 2025, followed by 3 days of casual leave from November 16 to 18. However, on November 13, the day before his leave began, he left his post ahead of schedule without submitting the required departure report.
On that day, Chakraborty concealed his identity and introduced himself as a DIG. He then used the DIG lounge and boarded a US-Bangla Airlines flight from Shah Makhdum Airport in Rajshahi to Dhaka at around 10:20am.
The notification further stated that he had used the VIP lounge at Rajshahi Airport several times before, identifying himself as “DIG, Rajshahi Range.” The matter came to the attention of various intelligence agencies, and the notification said his actions had severely damaged the police's image in the eyes of the public.
According to the Ministry of Home Affairs, these actions amounted to gross negligence in performing public duties, disregard for lawful orders and conduct contrary to departmental discipline. Under the Government Employees (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 2018, the actions constituted “misconduct,” a punishable offense.
A departmental case was filed against Chakraborty over the allegations. On February 5 this year, he was issued a show-cause notice along with a statement of allegations and a charge sheet. However, he did not submit a written reply within the stipulated time or apply for an extension.
The notification said an investigating officer was appointed on April 2 to examine the allegations. Following the investigation, a report was submitted on May 7, concluding that the misconduct charges against Chakraborty had been proven beyond doubt.
Based on the investigation report, a second show-cause notice was issued on June 16, asking why he should not be dismissed from service. He did not respond to that notice either.
The government subsequently reviewed the allegations, the investigation report and other documents before making a preliminary decision to dismiss Chakraborty from service.
The government then sought the opinion of the Bangladesh Public Service Commission, which recommended dismissal on September 14.
The matter was subsequently sent to the president for approval. On October 5, the president approved the dismissal proposal.
Accordingly, Chakraborty has been given the major penalty of dismissal from service under the relevant provisions of the Government Employees (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 2018.

item.title: Faqir Mahbub calls for global cooperation to ensure children’s online safety
item.description:
Minister of the Ministries for Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology, and Science and Technology Faqir Mahbub Anam has called for stronger global cooperation, joint initiatives among stakeholders and the exchange of international best practices to ensure children's safety in the digital environment.
He made the call while delivering Bangladesh's statement at the Business IT Breakfast titled "Digital Childhood Without Borders: Best International Practices for Child Safety Online", held in Moscow, Russia, on Thursday.
Representing Bangladesh at the event, the minister also conveyed, on behalf of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, his appreciation to the Global Digital Forum and the Alliance for the Protection of Children in the Digital Environment for undertaking this timely initiative.
Faqir Mahbub said Bangladesh is undergoing rapid digital transformation, enabling children to benefit from the online world for education and personal development.
At the same time, however, they are increasingly exposed to new and evolving forms of online risks, he added.
Ensuring children's digital safety is no longer the sole responsibility of parents or teachers; rather, it is a shared responsibility involving all stakeholders, including governments, online platforms, technology companies and civil society.
He said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, Bangladesh is working to strengthen relevant digital protection laws and legal frameworks, including the Cyber Security Act, to protect children's data and prevent online exploitation.
The minister, however, noted that such challenges cannot be addressed through legislation alone. In this regard, sharing international experiences, best practices and effective solutions that can be implemented on a broad scale is critically important, he said.
Referring to the review of the draft Joint Statement and Terms of Reference of the proposed Global Alliance to Protect Children in the Digital Environment, the minister congratulated the Russian Federation on taking this important initiative.
He further said the proposed document presents a comprehensive, child-rights-based framework in line with the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child.
The minister expressed Bangladesh's strong support for the three core principles of the proposed initiative, saying that the best interests of the child must be given the highest priority, the shared responsibility of all stakeholders must be ensured, and experiences and best practices must be exchanged through international cooperation.
He emphasized the importance of establishing a multilateral stakeholder framework that ensures equitable representation of different geographical regions, including the Asia-Pacific region.
Such a framework would provide opportunities for the realities, challenges and experiences of developing countries like Bangladesh to be appropriately reflected in the formulation of global strategies.
At the same time, Bangladesh welcomes the proposal to establish a Digital Childhood Safety Index and a dedicated platform for research and the exchange of best practices.
Faqir Mahbub Anam said enhancing digital literacy among children, parents and teachers is also a crucial foundation of the initiative.
He observed that developing the necessary knowledge and awareness in line with the rapid advancement of technologies, including artificial intelligence, could help establish an effective preventive mechanism against online harms.
He said Bangladesh remains firmly committed to the principles outlined in the Joint Statement of the Global Alliance to Protect Children in the Digital Environment.
Bangladesh is keen to work closely with the Alliance to protect children from online bullying, sexual harassment, data theft and other forms of digital harm.
The Alliance can play an important role in building a bridge between national policies and global cooperation, he added.
The telecommunications minister said Bangladesh is ready to work with all relevant stakeholders to build a future in which every child, regardless of nationality, can explore the digital world safely, creatively and without fear.
He said the collective initiative was an investment in future generations and that the digital future being built must be not only connected but also safe, inclusive and child-friendly.
Representatives from more than 100 countries participated in the international forum.

item.title: UK parliamentary delegation meets political and civil society leaders
item.description:
